sentences.text: No, clinician assessment for acute chest syndrome (ACS) in febrile patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) is not accurate enough, because physician sensitivity for predicting ACS was only 39%.
In a prospective study of 73 SCD patients with 96 febrile events, 24% (23/96) had CXR evidence of ACS, but 61% (14/23) of ACS cases were not clinically suspected before CXR.
No symptom or physical examination finding except splinting helped identify ACS, and 57% of patients with ACS had completely normal physical examination findings.
Diagnostic accuracy did not improve significantly with increasing levels of pediatric training.

Yes, the evidence indicates that perforation of the appendix is a risk factor for tubal infertility, with appendectomy also associated with ectopic pregnancy, though methodological limitations weaken the evidence.

A systematic review of four controlled studies found risk estimates ranging from 1.6 (95% CI 1.1–2.5) for ectopic pregnancy after appendectomy to 4.8 (95% CI 1.5–14.9) for tubal infertility from appendiceal perforation.
However, recall bias and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some reports weakened the validity of these findings.

In 153 acute stroke patients, those with NIHSS 0–5 had greater DWI lesion volumes for right than left strokes (mean 8.8 vs 3.2 cm3, P=0.04), and among lesions larger than 9 cm3, 8 of 37 right-sided strokes versus 1 of 39 left-sided strokes had NIHSS 0–5 (P=0.01); adjusted analysis also found lower acute NIHSS on the right for a given stroke volume (P=0.03).

In the NINDS t-PA placebo arm, right hemisphere stroke volume was greater than left after adjusting for baseline NIHSS (P<0.001), with right strokes roughly double the median volume of left strokes in each 5-point NIHSS category below 20 (e.g., NIHSS 16–20: 48 mL left vs 133 mL right, P<0.001).
Yes, a dedicated discharge coordinator improved some aspects of discharge quality, though the evidence is mixed by outcome.

In an intervention study of 600 randomly sampled adult medical patients discharged home from three medical wards, adding a discharge coordinator improved the discharge planning process, reduced problems patients experienced after discharge, and reduced perceived need for medical and healthcare services.
However, it did not improve timely or effective provision of community services after discharge or the appropriateness/efficiency of bed use.
A separate survey study concerned discharge information and coordination-of-care composites, not a dedicated discharge coordinator.

In an 11-year study of 241 bipolar disorder patients with three or more entries in a community mental health center management information system, the observed distribution of 1,224 manic and mixed episodes was compared with an expected distribution from 1,000 random simulations.
Episodes were consistent (all manic or all mixed) in significantly more patients than would be expected by chance.
The other supplied passages do not directly test this longitudinal consistency.
Yes, an observational study found that ST-segment ischaemic events were significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events in patients with ischaemic heart disease on hypotensive medications.

In 25 such patients, 107 hypotensive events were documented; 40 ST events occurred in 14 patients, and 14 hypotension-induced ischaemia events occurred in 8 patients, with 13 of 14 preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure and 6 by a fall in systolic pressure (chi2=11.9, p<0.001).

ST events were significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events (chi2=40.2, p<0.0001), and patients with these events were more often taking multiple hypotensive drug regimens (8/8 vs 9/17, p=0.022).
Yes—outcome in children with malignancy who develop acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) can be predicted from respiratory parameters.
In a retrospective review of 17 mechanically ventilated children with ARDS and malignancy (mean age 10.5 ± 5.1 years), 6 of 17 (35.3%) survived and sepsis syndrome was present in 70.6%.

Peak inspiratory pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure, and ventilation index values could distinguish outcome by day 3, while oxygenation efficiency (PaO2/FIO2 and P(A-a)O2) related significantly to outcome from day 8 after mechanical ventilation onset.

The evidence is mixed: delay in transfer to a rehabilitation unit for older patients with proximal femur fracture was associated with longer total hospital length of stay but did not predict discharge to a more dependent residence.
In an observational study of 455 patients aged over 75 years with proximal femur fracture, 58% were transferred to a rehabilitation ward.
Each day of delay in transfer was associated with a 0.64-day increase in total hospital length of stay (95% CI 0.23–1.05).
However, among transferred patients, only age over 85 years predicted discharge to a more dependent residence (relative risk 1.47, 95% CI 1.15–1.88), not delay in transfer.

One survey of 63 Canadian players (plus coaches from four levels) found that 62% of players believed headgear could prevent concussion versus 33% of coaches, but it assessed attitudes and wear, not whether headgear reduced concussions.

The other supplied studies examined pediatric emergency department concussion follow-up (ages 8-17) and bicycle-related injuries (1602 cases, 1540 controls; 141 concussions) and did not test rugby headgear; the bicyclist analysis found no association for concussion only.
Yes—in a retrospective comparative cohort, hospice enrollment among dying nursing home residents with daily pain was associated with improved pain management.
The study compared 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents with daily pain near the end of life across over 800 nursing homes.

Hospice residents were less likely to receive no analgesics (15% vs 23%; OR=0.57, 95% CI=0.45-0.74) and less likely to receive analgesics not recommended by AMDA (21% vs 29%; OR=0.65, 95% CI=0.52-0.80).
They were also more likely to receive regular treatment for daily pain (51% vs 33%; adjusted OR=2.08, 95% CI=1.68-2.56).
Yes—physiologic evidence indicates that mossy fibers release GABA.

In hippocampal slices from 3- to 5-week-old guinea pigs, electrical stimuli that recruit dentate granule cells elicited monosynaptic GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic signals in CA3 pyramidal neurons, and these signals met criteria for mossy fiber-CA3 synapses (metabotropic glutamate-receptor agonist sensitivity, facilitation during repetitive stimulation, and NMDA receptor-independent long-term potentiation).
Mossy fiber terminals also show intense GABA and GAD67 immunoreactivity, and the review's purpose was to present physiologic evidence of GABA release by mossy fibers.

The evidence is insufficient to establish increased neutrophil migratory activity after major trauma as a causal factor in the etiology of ARDS; the relevant study shows enhanced migration but does not directly link it to ARDS development.

In 17 adult blunt trauma patients with Injury Severity Score ≥18, neutrophils isolated at admission and 8 and 24 hours later migrated significantly more to interleukin-8 at 30 and 100 ng/mL than neutrophils from 9 normal volunteers (p<.05).

Neutrophil counts in whole blood were elevated at admission in patients who later developed ARDS and declined over 24 hours, but the migration results were not compared between patients who did and did not develop ARDS.
Thus, the study supports a plausible mechanism but does not prove that enhanced neutrophil migratory activity causes ARDS.
The evidence is mixed: cardiology-involving care was associated with better survival than general medicine alone, but cardiology-only care was not significantly better than combined care.
In a retrospective VHA cohort of 11,661 patients discharged with a primary diagnosis of CHF, 1-year mortality was lowest in the MIXED group (19%) and highest in the no-GM/CARD group (29%).
After adjustment, compared with MIXED care, the risk of death was 1.26 (1.15-1.38) for GM-only and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) for no-GM/CARD, while CARD-only was 1.12 (0.94-1.34).

The evidence is insufficient to establish that hepatitis G virus or TT virus are involved in cryptogenic chronic liver disease, because HGV and TTV markers were not significantly more frequent in cryptogenic disease than in HCV-related chronic liver disease.

In 23 patients with cryptogenic chronic liver disease versus 40 with HCV-related disease, HGV RNA was found in 4/23 (17.4%) versus 6/40 (15%, p=ns), any HGV marker in 6/23 (26.1%) versus 16/40 (40%, p=ns), and TTV-DNA in only 1 cryptogenic versus 2 HCV patients.
Demographic and clinical features, including liver histology, were comparable between HGV-infected and uninfected subjects, and severe liver damage was more frequent in HCV disease.
Other supplied passages note that the relevance of HGV/GBV-C in chronic hepatitis remains debated and that TTV status did not alter liver-specific biochemical parameters in hemodialysis patients.

Yes, pain is a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry, based on high prevalence and associated impairment/unfitness for work among psychiatric inpatients. In a cross-sectional questionnaire study of 106 patients primarily diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder in general adult psychiatry, point prevalence of pain was about 50%, 6-month prevalence 75.5%, and 12-month prevalence 76.5%. Almost 10% reported pain lasting at least 3 months in the past year, and impairment and unfitness for work were related to specific psychiatric diagnosis, with significant risk factors including depression (OR=6.05) and number of past psychiatric admissions (OR=3.609).
Yes, CT can help predict the level of CSF block in tuberculous hydrocephalus, but only through one finding: the shape of the third ventricle.

In a study of 50 children with communicating and 34 with non-communicating hydrocephalus confirmed by air-encephalography, the only CT index that correlated with the type of hydrocephalus was third-ventricle shape.
Significantly more children with non-communicating hydrocephalus had a rounded third ventricle than those with communicating hydrocephalus.
Yes, communication with terminally ill patients can be taught, based on a 2-day course that improved participants' self-assessed communication security and behavior.

In the first three courses, 31 participants showed growing sense of security across seven communication settings, with important increases for communicating cancer diagnoses with good or poor prognosis, recurrence, or far-progressive disease without curative approach.
Three months after the course, participants reported multiple changes indicating increased sensibility and professionalism in communication behavior.

Yes—among women treated with radiotherapy for Hodgkin's disease, treatment around the time of pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. In 382 women, the overall incidence was 16.0% in the pregnancy-associated group versus 2.3% in nonpregnant women (p=0.0001), and 10- and 15-year actuarial rates were 6.7% and 32.6% versus 0.4% and 1.7% (p=0.011). Multivariate analysis found pregnancy around radiotherapy was the only associated variable, with a hazard ratio of 22.49 (95% CI 5.56-90.88; p<0.001) for radiotherapy during pregnancy or within 1 month of pregnancy compared with nonpregnant women and those irradiated later than 1 month after pregnancy.

Yes, preclinical evidence supports c-Kit-dependent growth in uveal melanoma and identifies it as a potential therapeutic target, based on a study showing c-kit expression, phosphorylation, and sensitivity to the c-kit inhibitor STI571.

In that study, c-kit was expressed in 84 of 134 paraffin-embedded uveal melanoma specimens and 6 of 8 fresh-frozen samples, and was strongly expressed and tyrosine-phosphorylated in three uveal melanoma cell lines (OCM-1, OCM-3, 92-1) compared with cutaneous melanoma cells.

The same cell lines produced the c-kit ligand (stem cell growth factor), suggesting autocrine/paracrine stimulation, and treatment with STI571 blocked c-kit autophosphorylation and caused cell death with an IC50 <2.5 microM for both phosphorylation and proliferation.

The evidence is mixed: an exploratory meta-analysis of two randomized controlled trials in stroke patients found a definite relationship between maximum reduction in arm spasticity and maximum improvement in arm function, independent of treatment, but the relationship was clear only for certain botulinum toxin doses.

In 137 patients, the correlation between maximum change in spasticity and maximum change in arm function was rho = -0.2822 (p = 0.0008); for botulinum toxin (Dysport) at 500 units it was rho = -0.5679 (p = 0.0090, n = 22) and at 1000 units rho = -0.4430 (p = 0.0018, n = 47), but no significant relationship was seen with placebo or 1500 units.
Maximum changes in spasticity and function occurred concurrently in 47 patients, with spasticity improvement preceding functional improvement in 26 and the reverse in 18.
The evidence is insufficient to conclude that combining 2-methoxyestradiol with chemotherapy can reduce chemotherapeutic dosages in human ovarian cancer treatment.

In two human ovarian cancer cell lines, 2ME (0.8-25 microM) combined with epirubicine, doxorubicine, paclitaxel, docetaxel, carboplatin, vinorelbine, 5-fluorouracil, or mafosfamide produced a significant additive antiproliferative effect only with epirubicine and carboplatin, at the lower concentration range of those chemotherapeutics.

Bottom line: yes, preoperative tracheobronchoscopy matters in newborns with esophageal atresia because it was clinically useful in 45.2% and crucially modified the surgical approach in 24.2% of patients.

In a series of 62 newborns with EA who underwent preoperative flexible tracheobronchoscopy while breathing spontaneously, TBS identified unsuspected proximal fistula in 3 of 9 type A patients, previously undetected respiratory tree malformations in 4 patients, and allowed Fogarty catheter occlusion of carinal fistulas in 14 type C patients.
Overall, TBS was clinically useful in 28/62 (45.2%) and crucial in modifying the surgical approach in 15/62 (24.2%), with no complications observed.
No, the one direct test found no significant gender differences in self-report of depression symptoms, suggesting differential symptom reporting does not account for higher depression rates in women.

In a population-based 13-year follow-up of 1,727 community-dwelling adults in East Baltimore, women were no more likely than men to endorse sadness after adjustment for age, ethnicity, education, marital status, and employment (adjusted direct effect 0.105, 95% CI -0.113 to 0.323).

Other passages confirm higher reported rates of depression and anxiety in women and show higher depression rates for females only in some alcohol-use-disorder symptom patterns , but they do not directly test differential symptom reporting.
Thus the evidence suggests the higher rates are not accounted for by differential symptom reporting, though this conclusion rests mainly on the single direct study.

No, increased private health care use was not associated with reduced NHS demand in a UK study; NHS referral rates were significantly higher (rate ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.71, p=0.001) in wards with private referral rates in the top fifth compared with the bottom fifth after adjustment for deprivation and practice.

The study included 17,137 referrals from 10 general practices, with 90.4% to the NHS and 9.6% to the private sector, and private referral rates were lower in deprived areas (rate ratio 0.25, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.41).
No, decisional algorithms cannot replace global introspection in the individual causality assessment of spontaneously reported ADRs, because they had low specificity despite high sensitivity.
In 500 adverse reports, an expert panel assessed causality using WHO global introspection while the same reports were independently assessed with 15 published algorithms.
The algorithms averaged 93% sensitivity and 89% positive predictive value but only 7% specificity and 31% negative predictive value.
This indicates they would misclassify many non-drug-related reports as drug related, so they are not a replacement for global introspection in individual assessment.
No, endoaortic balloon occlusion was not shown to be safe in this setting; it was associated with significantly higher in-hospital mortality.

In 52 of 2,172 consecutive patients selected for endoaortic occlusion because of aortic calcifications or epiaortic ultrasound findings, 10 (19.2%) required conversion to conventional cross-clamping for incomplete occlusion, hindered exposure, or balloon rupture.

In-hospital death occurred in 13 patients (25%) versus 4.2% in all other patients (p<0.0001), and multivariable analysis found endoaortic occlusion independently associated with death (OR 5.609, 95% CI 2.684–11.719); stroke was 3.8% versus 0.8% (p=0.067).

The evidence is mixed and group-dependent: in a French study, breaching confidentiality to protect a wife from a patient's sexually transmitted disease was rated more acceptable by lay people and psychologists than by physicians (mean ratings 11.76, 9.28, and 2.90, respectively, on a 0-22 scale).

The study included 144 lay people, 10 psychologists, and 7 physicians judging 48 scenarios, and found the patient's stated intentions to protect and inform his wife had the greatest impact on acceptability.
Lay participants were not uniform: 14 found it always acceptable, 87 said it depended on many circumstances, 30 required consultation with an expert, and 13 found it never acceptable.
Thus the passages show qualified acceptability, especially among lay people and psychologists, but low acceptability among physicians and substantial variation by circumstances.

In a Swedish population-based cohort of 2,787 mother-daughter pairs and 831 sister pairs with breast cancer diagnosed from 1961 to 2001, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor 5-year prognosis had a 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality than those of a proband with good prognosis (HR, 1.6; 95% CI, 1.2-2.2; p for trend 0.002).
Five-year survival was 87% versus 91% for daughters depending on maternal outcome, and 70% versus 88% for sisters.
The other supplied passages concern pancreatic cancer predisposition or secular breast cancer prognosis, not inherited breast cancer prognosis.
Bottom line: the evidence suggests bile duct sludge is not clearly different from bile duct stones in recurrence after endoscopic clearance, although some associated features differ.
In 228 patients undergoing therapeutic ERCP for suspected choledocholithiasis, bile duct sludge without stones occurred in 14% (31/228) and was more common in females.

After endoscopic clearance, recurrent CBD stones occurred in 16% (5/31) of patients with bile duct sludge versus 17% (33/197) of patients with CBD stones (p = 0.99), and other risk factors were not statistically different.
However, common bile duct dilation was less common in the sludge group.
The other supplied passages address different populations and do not directly compare bile duct sludge with bile duct stones.

Yes, reading comprehension ability can be improved in adults with mild intellectual disabilities, based on a study showing substantial transfer effects to general text comprehension after strategy instruction. The study included 38 adults with ID (age 20-72 years, mean 36; IQ 45-69, mean 58) who received 15 weekly 1-hour lessons over 3 months teaching summarizing, questioning, clarifying, and predicting strategies. Results showed no significant difference between individual and small-group instruction, but direct strategy effects were substantial except for questioning, and the transfer effect to general text comprehension was even more substantial and maintained at follow-up. General reading comprehension variance was best explained by sentence reading comprehension and only moderately by the strategies trained.

One study in managed care patients from west coast physician organizations aimed to test whether observed changes in health-related quality of life over 2.5 years reflect process of care, but no results or effect estimates are provided.
A separate analysis of adults with chronic disease characterized 347,606 patients and 7,662,411 ambulatory visits and examined access patterns, not HRQOL outcomes.
Other supplied passages link primary care quality to emergency department costs or compare QOL by treatment setting, but they do not test ambulatory process of care as a predictor of HRQOL.
The evidence is mixed: a statistically significant but clinically weak association was found, while the top-versus-bottom ACE quartile difference was not statistically significant.

In 300 people with Type 1 diabetes not taking renin-angiotensin system blockers, severe hypoglycaemia incidence was 0.93 episodes per patient-year; the top and bottom ACE quartiles had 0.5 versus 1.7 episodes per patient-year (P=0.075), Spearman r=0.115 (P=0.047), and a negative binomial model was significant (P=0.002) but clinically weak.
Other supplied passages address hypoglycaemia unawareness with ACE inhibitor/ARB use and ADR-related hospital episodes, not serum ACE and severe hypoglycaemia frequency in Type 1 diabetes.

Yes, adjuvant aromatase inhibitors appear to increase cardiovascular risk compared with tamoxifen in early breast cancer, based on a report of an unexpectedly greater number of grade 3 and 4 cardiovascular events.
Yes, surgical management appears necessary because viable germ cell elements were found in 14% of testicular remnants from patients with vanishing testes syndrome.

In a retrospective review of 56 patients (age 11–216 months) who had spermatic vessels and a vas deferens exiting a closed internal inguinal ring, 8 of 56 specimens (14%) contained viable germ cell elements, and an additional 4 (7%) had seminiferous tubules without germ cell elements.
These histologic findings support removal of the remnant, although the passage does not explicitly state the malignant potential of those elements.

Yes, routine laboratory markers appear useful for distinguishing nonalcoholic from alcoholic steatohepatitis, with a multivariate model including MCV, AST/ALT ratio, and sex achieving an aROC of 0.92.

In 95 biopsy-confirmed steatohepatitis patients (58 NASH, 37 ASH), an AST/ALT ratio >1 was more common in ASH (54.1% vs 20.7%, P=0.0008), and elevated MCV occurred in 53% of ASH patients but was normal in all NASH patients (P<0.0001).
High-grade fibrosis was also more frequent in ASH (59% vs 19%, P<0.0001), and MCV differences were more marked in high-grade fibrosis.

No—the evidence suggests specialised phonological-awareness training is not indicated for every preschool child as a universal intervention, because in a prospective study the whole group showed only a slight difference between specialised phonological-awareness training and general-perception training in later writing abilities.

That study enrolled 218 preschool children and compared 131 after first grade; the specialised program produced the greatest reading benefit specifically in children with a history of hearing loss, actual hearing loss, or pathologic middle-ear findings.
The other supplied passages do not evaluate this question in a general preschool population.
The evidence is insufficient to establish a diagnostic role for c-kit expression in HBV-induced chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma.

In a retrospective immunohistochemical study of 125 HBV-infected patients (25 each with mild, moderate, severe hepatitis, cirrhosis, and HCC) plus 50 additional HBV-related HCCs, c-kit positivity was greatest in severe hepatitis and HCC, and c-kit expression was found in 62 of 75 HCC specimens (82%, p<0.001).
Cirrhotic livers showed lower staining intensity and rare c-kit positivity, while staining intensity paralleled grade and stage in chronic hepatitis B.

In a retrospective study of 154 adults undergoing esophagectomy, partial or total gastrectomy, redo Heller myotomy, or redo/transthoracic fundoplication, 14 developed new-onset atrial fibrillation; laparoscopic surgery was associated with lower risk (p = 0.004), and multivariate analysis showed an odds ratio of 0.09 (95% CI 0.01-0.95, p = 0.04) after adjusting for surgery type.

In 42 pregnancies with severe Kell alloimmunization, fetal thrombocytopenia (<150 x10^9/L) occurred in 4/42 (10%), but none had a platelet count <50 x10^9/L, including 15 with severe hydrops; in contrast, RhD alloimmunized controls had higher rates of thrombocytopenia (84/318, 26% <150 x10^9/L; 2/230 non-hydropic and 7/30 severely hydropic with <50 x10^9/L).
The other supplied study focuses on perinatal mortality and screening, not fetal platelet counts.

Yes, pectins appear to be involved in cold acclimation and de-acclimation of winter oil-seed rape, based on cold-induced increases in cell wall and pectin contents and low-methylated pectin, with de-acclimation reversing most of these effects except pectin methylesterase activity.
The study used leaves of two double-haploid winter oil-seed rape (Brassica napus subsp. oleifera) lines differing in winter survival and blackleg resistance.

Cold acclimation at 2 degrees C retarded leaf expansion and increased freezing resistance, tensile stiffness, cell wall and pectin contents, pectin methylesterase activity, and low-methylated pectin independently of genotype.
De-acclimation promoted leaf expansion and reversed most cold-induced effects, except pectin methylesterase activity.

Yes—home sampling kits for bacterial sexually transmitted infections were generally viewed as positive by men who have sex with men (MSM) in a qualitative study. In focus groups (n=20) and one-to-one interviews (n=24) with MSM, participants identified benefits including increased access to testing, enhanced personal comfort, and empowerment. Concerns raised included test accuracy, delays in receiving results, possible lack of support, and potential negative impact on others.

The evidence suggests no—or at least that hormonal/reproductive-age differences are not the sole explanation—because female gender protection remained unchanged in both young (<48 yrs) and old (>52 yrs) women after injury with hemorrhagic shock.

In a cohort of 1,036 blunt-injured adults with hemorrhagic shock (680 men, 356 women; mean ISS 32 +/- 14), female gender was independently associated with a 43% lower risk of multiple organ failure and a 23% lower risk of nosocomial infection after confounder adjustment.
Gender remained an independent risk factor in young and old subgroup analysis, with the protection afforded by female gender remaining unchanged.
The passages characterize the dimorphism but do not directly measure hormones, so they do not prove which hormonal mechanisms, if any, are responsible.
The evidence is mixed and context-dependent, so there is no single answer to whether it is better to be big.
For tissue microarray cores, a single random 0.6-mm spot was comparable to whole 1-mm or 1.5-mm cores (Pearson R 0.87-0.98), and there is no evidence that large cores are better than small cores.

For body size, overweight and obese girls selected larger ideal body figures and had better food choice intentions than non-overweight peers, but many overweight/obese adults misperceived their weight and 20% did not think their health would improve with weight loss.
Yes, the zeolite hemostatic agent QuikClot-Advanced Clotting Sponge reduced blood loss during arterial injury in a swine model.

In 16 swine with a 5 mm femoral artery incision, the control group (n=6) received a pressure dressing with manual pressure, while the QC group (n=10) had QC applied directly over the lacerated femoral artery.
Application of QC led to decreased total blood loss and significantly higher hematocrit levels, along with a slower drop in blood pressure.
The study also noted significant heat production and mild edematous and vacuolar changes in nerve samples.

Yes—survey evidence suggests ESC can change how some people drive: 23% of ESC owners who knew their vehicle had ESC reported noticing long-lasting changes in their driving behavior since they began driving the vehicle.

This rests on a telephone survey of 1,017 owners/drivers of 2006–2008 ESC-equipped passenger vehicles in Quebec and British Columbia, Canada, and no direct comparison group was reported for that behavioral-change item.

The evidence is mixed: in a national sample of 3,939 veterans with ischemic stroke, overall performance was >70% for 10 of 14 inpatient quality indicators, but older patients were less likely than younger patients to receive some processes of care.

After adjustment, age-related differences were less consistent, though the oldest patients remained less likely to receive lipid management and the youngest were more likely to receive smoking cessation counseling.

Thus, the passages show generally high performance on most measured indicators but persistent age differences on some, so they do not settle whether older patients receive adequate stroke care overall.

In 994 men without prostate cancer (4,937 observations) in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, body mass index was not significantly associated with prostate specific antigen after age adjustment (p = 0.06), with a 10-point body mass index increase linked to only -0.03 ng/ml difference (95% CI -0.40-0.49).

In 6,103 men undergoing 2-year biopsy, mean adjusted prostate specific antigen decreased across normal weight, overweight, and obese groups on placebo (7.73, 7.17, 6.79 ng/ml; p-trend=0.192) and on dutasteride (3.16, 2.93, 2.62 ng/ml; p=0.008), but the AUC for predicting prostate cancer did not differ across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥0.212).
The evidence is mixed: in a proof-of-concept randomized trial, fenofibrate improved some sleep apnoea indices but did not significantly change the apnoea/hypopnoea index (AHI).

In 34 subjects with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with CPAP (mean age 55 years, BMI 34 kg/m2, fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L), 4 weeks of fenofibrate 145 mg daily versus placebo significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO2<90% (9.0% to 3.5% vs 10.0% to 11.5%, p=0.007), obstructive apnoeas (by 44%, 18.5 to 15.0 vs 29.0 to 30.5, p=0.048), and non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour (23.5 to 18.0 vs 24.0 to 25.0, p=0.004).
However, the AHI change was not significant (14% reduction vs control, 95% CI -47 to 40%, p=0.533), and other sleep variables were not significantly influenced.

The only relevant supplied report describes a seven-year-old girl with probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome, microcephaly, mental retardation, recurrent infections, and cerebro-mediastinal tuberculosis, but her extensive immunological work-up was normal and the authors only discuss a putative causative link.
Other supplied passages address ESR in childhood TB, ADA/CT patterns in TB, and streptococcal infections with neuropsychiatric disorders, none of which test this specific association.
Thus, the passages do not settle the question and show only a single co-occurrence, not causation.

Among 692 women at 24–32 weeks' gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids at one institution, 46.4% delivered within 1 week and 13.3% within 24 hours, while only 124 (17.9%) remained pregnant 1 week after corticosteroids and delivered at <34 weeks.

Those remaining pregnant and delivering at <34 weeks were more likely to have received corticosteroids for premature preterm rupture of membranes (OR 3.83, 95% CI 2.06–7.17), twins (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.42–5.95), or before 28 weeks (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.38–3.52).
Yes, the evidence indicates that scale matters for identifying racial disparities in breast cancer mortality.

In a Texas study (1995-2005), the proportion and location of significant racial disparities among African-American, Hispanic, and White non-Hispanic women changed depending on whether relative risk or risk difference was used and on the geographic level (census tract, zip code, or county).
The largest proportion of significant results was observed for the risk difference statistic and census tract data.

African-American and Hispanic women generally had higher mortality than White non-Hispanics, especially in southeast metropolitan areas and the southwest border, and significant disparity regions often had poverty rates above 10.00%.
Other supplied studies address race as a prognostic factor or breast-conserving surgery but do not test geographic scale.

In the only relevant study, 61 elderly patients with polymyalgic syndrome were followed for 1 year; 32 (52%) had a diagnostic shift, and baseline ultrasound findings predicted the eventual diagnosis of PMR rather than prognosis, with subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis (OR 5.603, p=0.003) and low frequency of wrist, metacarpophalangeal, and metatarsophalangeal effusion/synovitis predicting PMR.
The remaining supplied passages address prognosis in multiple sclerosis and psychiatric relapse, not polymyalgia rheumatica.

Yes, the Turkish version of the EQ-5D showed evidence of construct validity in patients with acute coronary syndrome, based on a cross-sectional study. In 122 ACS patients (mean age 62.9±9.3 years, 72.1% male), EQ-5D index scores correlated with MacNew heart-related quality-of-life subscales (Spearman r=0.557–0.721) and EQ-5D VAS scores correlated with MacNew subscales (r=0.297–0.484), all p<0.001. In stepwise regression, the MacNew global score was a significant predictor of EQ-5D index score (β=0.188; 95% CI 0.152–0.224; p<0.001).
Yes, endometrial polyp formation is associated with increased expression of VEGF and TGF-β1 in a study comparing polyps with adjacent endometrium in 70 premenopausal women.
VEGF was significantly higher in polyp glandular cells in both proliferative (P<0.001) and secretory (P=0.03) phases, and in stromal cells in the proliferative phase (P=0.006).
TGF-β1 was significantly higher in polyp glandular cells in the proliferative phase (P=0.02) and in stromal cells in both proliferative (P=0.006) and secretory (P=0.008) phases.
Thus the evidence supports an association, though the increases varied by cell type and menstrual cycle phase.
Yes, the association varies by gender, but it is largely accounted for by living arrangement.

In the Swiss National Cohort of all residents over age 44 (n=2,440,242), the mortality benefit of being married was stronger for men than women, and after adjustment for living arrangements the gender difference by marital status disappeared.

Among 45-64-year-olds, the highest mortality risks were for divorced men living alone (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.67 to 1.76) and single men living alone (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.63 to 1.71), whereas for women the highest risk was for those single and living with a partner (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58 to 1.82).
In older age groups, the impact of marital status decreased.
No, the available evidence indicates that delivery mode did not significantly affect postpartum quality of life among women in rural China.

In a cross-sectional household survey of women residing in rural areas and 0–12 months after childbirth from 30 rural townships, none of the six quality-of-life dimensions or the total score differed significantly between women who had normal delivery and those who had caesarean section.

The overall caesarean section rate was 70.0% (962/1375), yet the study found that postnatal home visits were related to good quality of life, while lower husband education and male infant gender were associated with poor quality of life.
The other supplied passage focuses on NCMS reimbursement and delivery service utilization, not postpartum quality of life.

The evidence is mixed: some differences in care needs and preferences exist between elderly and younger cancer patients, but a direct needs assessment found few significant differences apart from intimacy and support.

In that cross-sectional study of cancer patients aged 35–82 divided into ≤65 and ≥66 years, the older group most often requested financial-insurance information (73.9%), contact with people with the same illness (71.7%), more comprehensible information from doctors and nurses (71.7%), and better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%), yet few significant differences emerged between age subgroups except for needs such as intimacy and support.

In another comparison of <65 versus 65+ gynecologic cancer cohorts, treatment modalities were similar (P=0.28) and diagnosis differed (P<0.001), while the elderly more strongly desired cure when treatment involved disfigurement (P=0.029), younger patients rated sexuality/femininity issues as more important (P<0.001), and the elderly more strongly believed doctors should make management decisions (P<0.001).

One study evaluated a slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based method for pupil diameter in 40 healthy eyes, reporting a mean diameter of 5.81 ± 0.70 mm with SLBM versus 6.26 ± 0.68 mm with Colvard infrared pupillometry, but it did not specify mesopic conditions or cobalt blue light.
The other supplied passage concerns slitlamp measurement of the disc-foveal angle, not pupil size.
No, the distribution of health care benefits in Kenya did not meet the principles of universal coverage, because benefits were distributed on the basis of ability to pay and not on need for care.

Using nationally representative household surveys from 2003 and 2007 and benefit incidence analysis across public, private-not-for-profit, and private-for-profit sectors, the study found that all three sectors had similar pro-rich distribution in 2003; by 2007 the private-not-for-profit sector was pro-poor and the public sector was equal, but the private-for-profit sector remained pro-rich.
It also found larger pro-rich disparities for inpatient than outpatient benefits at the hospital level, while primary health care services were pro-poor.

In 30 guinea pigs, control animals showed no cochlear changes, whereas therapeutic-dose halofantrine caused loss and distortion of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells plus loss of spiral ganglia cells, and double-dose halofantrine distorted inner and outer hair cells and caused loss of spiral ganglia cells.
The same report notes there have been no studies investigating halofantrine's effect on hearing in humans.
Yes, increased carotid artery pulsatility and resistance indexes appear to be early sonographic signs of vascular abnormalities in young obese males.
This rests on a study comparing 35 young obese males with 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers.
In that study, the mean common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were statistically higher in obese subjects than in healthy controls.

Yes, the study demonstrated that laser pretreatment enhanced transdermal absorption of topical lidocaine in an in vivo pig model, supporting the concept for fractional lasers. In four pigs, 4% topical lidocaine was applied under occlusion for 60 minutes to a 400 cm2 abdominal area before and after Er:YAG laser treatment at 500, 250, 50, and 25 µm depths. Serum lidocaine and MEGX were undetectable in untreated skin but detectable after laser treatment, with peak lidocaine significantly higher at 250 µm (0.62 mg/L) than at 500 µm (0.45 mg/L), 50 µm (0.48 mg/L), or 25 µm (0.3 mg/L) (P=0.0002), and peak MEGX also highest at 250 µm (0.048 mg/L) (P≤0.0001).
No, global management at the same centre did not improve results in a retrospective study of colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases.
In that study, 45 GM patients and 66 SM patients had similar 3-year (51% vs 67%) and 5-year (31% vs 35%) overall survival, both non-significant.

Five-year disease-free survival was higher with separate management (14% vs 11%, P=0.009), while GM was associated with fewer mean procedures (1.6 vs 2.3) and more first-step liver resections during colorectal surgery (62% vs 6%).

The evidence is mixed: DaTSCAN generally separates essential tremor (ET) from Parkinson's disease (PD), but a semiquantitative striatal reduction in ET and one equivocal case leave a small possibility of dopaminergic overlap.

In a study of 28 ET patients, 28 normal volunteers (NV), and 33 PD patients, qualitative DaTSCAN showed no difference in striatal, caudate, or putamen uptake between ET and NV, whereas all PD patients had reduced putamen uptake.
Semiquantitatively, ET patients had significantly lower striatal uptake than NV, and PD patients had reduced putamen uptake compared with ET and NV.

Clinical follow-up of 20 ET patients showed no significant change or signs of PD, and repeat DaTSCAN in 10 was negative in all but one, who had an equivocal baseline scan that deteriorated 12 months later.

The evidence is mixed and comes from a single intensive care medicine study, in which open access status independently predicted more citations but the overall median citation difference was not statistically significant.
That study evaluated 161 articles published in Intensive Care Medicine in 2008, 76% of which were non-open access, and compared citation counts through April 30, 2011.

Median citations were 8 (4-12) for non-open access versus 9 (6-18) for open access (p=0.084), while among the highest-cited articles (>8 citations) the counts were 13 (10-16) versus 18 (13-21) (p=0.008), and open access status was an independent factor for citation advantage (β=3.618; p=0.006).

In a study of 40 patients and 20 asymptomatic volunteers (120 temporomandibular joints), static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound had considerably lower sensitivity compared with MRI for detecting disk displacement, with technical difficulties from limited access due to surrounding bone structures.
Other supplied studies evaluated CT in rheumatoid arthritis , hyaluronic acid injections or splints , and clinical assessment versus MRI , but none assessed ultrasound.
Yes, a porcine training model for retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) was developed to teach and practice the procedure.
In this model, 15 piglets underwent RPN with three ports; operative time ranged from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30 minutes) and blood loss from 5 to 100 mL (median 20 mL).

Comparing the first eight cases (group A) with the last seven (group B) showed significant improvement in peritoneal opening (p=0.025), operative time (p=0.0037), and blood loss (p=0.026), with an experimental learning curve of eight cases.
The evidence is mixed: obesity at the start of adolescence was associated with greater prevalence and persistence of wheezing by age 15, but not with incident wheezing.
In the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort, 4,349 individuals were followed from ages 10-11 to 14-15 years, and wheezing was defined by the ISAAC questionnaire.

Independent of confounders, the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was 50% greater among those obese at 11 years than among eutrophic individuals (RR 1.53; 95% CI: 1.14-2.05), and the risk of persistent wheezing among obese individuals at 11 years was 1.82 (95% CI: 1.30-2.54).
However, weight status and skinfolds showed no association with incident wheezing.

Yes, a meta-analysis of four RCTs (321 patients) found operative treatment superior to nonoperative treatment for displaced midshaft clavicular fractures, with lower rates of nonunion (95% CI 0.05-0.43, P=0.0004), malunion (95% CI 0.06-0.34, P<0.00001), and overall complications (95% CI 0.43-0.76, P=0.0001).
Operative treatment also significantly reduced neurologic symptoms (95% CI 0.20-0.74, P=0.004) and dissatisfaction with appearance (95% CI 0.19-0.65, P=0.001).
Functional outcomes were improved with surgery (P<0.05), but the analysis was limited by lack of consistent standardized assessment data.

The evidence is insufficient to determine whether etoricoxib is effective in preventing heterotopic ossification after primary total hip arthroplasty, resting on a single-arm phase-2 study with no control group.

In 42 patients undergoing cemented primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis who took oral etoricoxib 90 mg for seven days, 62% had no heterotopic ossification at six months, while 31% had Brooker grade 1 and 7% had Brooker grade 2 ossification.
The survival difference was significant in node-positive patients (32.0% vs 12.7%, P=0.004) but not in node-negative patients (68.6% vs 58.8%, P=0.085).

The evidence is insufficient to call sternal skin conductance a reasonable surrogate for hot flash measurement, and the only relevant pilot found poor concordance between self-reported and device-recorded hot flashes.

In that study, 16 women wore the second SSC prototype for 5 weeks; the first prototype collected no analyzable data due to malfunction, and the second prototype showed only 24% concordance with self-reported hot flashes.
Yes, limited evidence suggests lumbar drainage is effective for postoperative CSF fistula after spine surgery, based on faster wound healing in a small series.
In 198 spine surgery patients, 16 (8%) developed postoperative CSF fistulas; 10 were treated with external CSF lumbar drainage for 10 days and 6 conservatively with prone positioning for 3 weeks.
All patients healed properly with no adverse events, and the drainage group healed in a mean of 10 days versus 30 days for conservative treatment.

Other supplied passages do not directly address this spine-surgery population: one reports a postoperative CSF leak treated with 4 days of lumbar drainage but does not specify spine surgery , while the others concern sacral nerve root cysts and endoscopic CSF rhinorrhea repair.

Yes—an implant coating with antibacterial-loaded hydrogel reduced bacterial colonization and biofilm formation in vitro, based on the DAC hydrogel combined with various antibacterials showing bactericidal and antibiofilm effects in vitro.
In that in vitro testing, complete release of all tested antibacterial compounds occurred within less than 96 hours.
Approximately 80% of the hydrogel coating was retrieved on the implant after press-fit insertion, though that was in rabbit tibias and human femurs rather than an in vitro biofilm assay.

No, HFNC were not noisier than bubble CPAP in preterm infants; average noise at the external auditory meatus showed no evidence of a difference, with a mean difference of -1.6 dBA (95% CI -4.0 to 0.9) for HFNC compared with BCPAP.
In 21 preterm infants with 21 HFNC and 13 BCPAP measurements, HFNC at 500 Hz was actually 3.0 dBA quieter (95% CI 0.3 to 5.7).
Noise increased with increasing BCPAP gas flow (p=0.007) but not with set pressure, and there was a trend toward increased noise with higher HFNC flow.
Yes, in a dog experiment solitary kidneys were more resistant to warm ischemia than paired kidneys, showing less functional decline and less tubular necrosis.

In that study 10 dogs with a solitary kidney after right nephrectomy and 10 dogs with both kidneys underwent 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion; solitary-kidney dogs had a 20% clearance decrease at 1 week and regained basal function by week 2, whereas paired-kidney dogs had >90% clearance decrease up to week 2 and a 23% reduction at 4 weeks.

Histopathology showed 60% tubular necrosis at 3 days in solitary kidneys versus 90% in paired kidneys, with regeneration starting at 1 week versus 2 weeks, and proinflammatory markers were higher and more sustained in paired kidneys.
However, the authors noted there were no evidence-based medicine data to critically judge this vulnerability in humans, so the human clinical answer remains uncertain.
Yes, specific IgE determination by ISAC 112 is generally reproducible, though with some variability across batches and laboratories.

In a study of 20 samples (19 polysensitized allergic patients and the manufacturer's calibrator CTR02), measured ten times in the same and different assays and tested in two laboratories and two kit batches, intra- and inter-assay agreement was very good for 94 allergens and good for one.

Inter-batch agreement was very good for 82 allergens, good for 14, moderate for 5, poor for 1, and bad for 1, while inter-laboratory agreement was very good for 73, good for 22, moderate for 6, and poor for 2.
The mean coefficient of variation was 9.4% for CTR02 but 22.9% for patient sera, indicating greater variability in patient samples.

No—concomitant anterior/apical repair during midurethral sling did not improve the overactive bladder symptom component of mixed urinary incontinence more than sling alone in a retrospective cohort. In 151 women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence, 67 underwent midurethral sling only and 84 underwent midurethral sling plus anterior/apical repair, with the Overactive Bladder Questionnaire Symptom Severity score change measured 6 weeks after surgery. The OAB-q SS change score was 30 ± 26 for sling-only versus 25 ± 25 for sling plus anterior/apical repair (p = 0.20), and multivariate regression showed no difference between groups, indicating similar improvements in OAB symptoms. Thus, the passages show no additional OAB benefit from concomitant repair, although lower change scores were associated with postoperative complications.
In 87 AMD patients (45 wet, 42 dry) and 80 healthy controls from Turkey, the genotype distributions of these HIF1A SNPs did not differ significantly between cases and controls.
The only significant association found was for CFH rs1061170, where at least one C allele increased AMD risk (OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.22-4.81).
The evidence is insufficient to establish that vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency is related to the development of osteochondritis dissecans.

In a prospective pilot study of 23 consecutive patients (12 male, 11 female) with stage III or III/IV OCD lesions and a mean age of 31.3 years, 18 of 23 had a distinct vitamin D3 deficiency, 2 were vitamin D3-insufficient, and 3 had the lowest normal vitamin D3 value.

The evidence is mixed but does show correlations between some androgens and sexual desire in women, since a cross-sectional study found sexual desire correlated overall with free testosterone and androstenedione in 560 healthy women aged 19-65.

In the subgroup aged 25-44 with no systemic hormonal contraception, sexual desire correlated with total testosterone, free testosterone, androstenedione, and DHEAS, while in women aged 45-65 only androstenedione correlated.
No correlation was found between ADT-G and sexual desire.

The same report notes that the correlation between circulating androgens and sexual desire is inconclusive and that androgen substitution improves sexual function in women with decreased desire due to surgical menopause, pituitary disease, or age-related ovarian androgen decline.
No, only a minority of elderly patients correctly endorsed calling 911 for clinical scenarios suggestive of acute stroke.

In a cross-sectional study of 367 elderly out-patients (≥60 years) in Buenos Aires, only 14% correctly endorsed intention to call 911 on the Stroke Action Test (cut-off ≥75%), and only 65% reported they would call an ambulance for the most typical stroke signs and symptoms.
On average, the correct response was chosen only 37% of the time, and the least-recognized symptom (amaurosis fugax) prompted calling in just 15%.
Yes, bone thickness and inter-radicular space can affect miniscrew placement in posterior mandibular sites; a CBCT study measured these variables and found bone thickness varied with insertion angle.

In 100 orthodontic patients (61 female, 39 male; mean age 17.4 ± 6.74 years; 60 Class I and 40 Class II molar relationships), inter-radicular space was evaluated 5 mm from the cement-enamel junction and bone thickness was simulated at 45°, 60°, and 90° insertion angles.
Inter-radicular space ranged from 2.46 to 3.31 mm and alveolar bone thickness ranged from 8.01 to 13.77 mm, with thickness decreasing as the insertion angle increased from 45° to 90°.
No significant differences were found between genders or malocclusion types.

The evidence is mixed: loss of DKK3 is associated with lymph node metastasis in gastric cancer, and adding DKK3 status to CT improved prediction of lymph node involvement from 71.5% to 80.0% in advanced gastric cancer, but the study assessed DKK3 on gastrectomy specimens rather than preoperative samples.
In 158 gastric cancer patients who underwent gastrectomy, loss of DKK3 expression was found in 64 (40.5%) and was significantly associated with lymph node metastasis (p<0.001).
Based on preoperative CT staging, the combination of DKK3 expression status and CT increased accuracy for predicting lymph node involvement in AGC patients.
However, because DKK3 expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry on surgical samples, these data do not directly demonstrate that preoperative DKK3 testing can predict lymph node metastasis.
Yes, a retrospective case-control study found that failures of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) were associated with steeper posterior tibial slopes (PTS).
In 20 ACLR failure cases and 20 randomly selected controls from 238 patients, the odds ratio for ACLR failure was 6.8 for medial PTS ≥5° (P=0.007) and 10.8 for lateral PTS ≥5° (P=0.000).
5.5° for failure vs. control groups, which appear reversed relative to the stated conclusion, but the overall findings support an association.

No, the probability of prenatal diagnosis (PND) or termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly (TOPFA) does not differ significantly between ART-conceived and spontaneously conceived fetuses with congenital heart defects.

In a population-based study of fetuses with CHD in Paris, PND was 28.1% for ART-conceived (n=171) versus 34.6% for spontaneously conceived (n=4620) fetuses (P=0.077), and TOPFA was 36.2% versus 39.2% (P=0.677), with similar estimates after adjustment for confounders.
Gestational age at PND tended to be earlier for ART fetuses (23.1 vs 24.8 weeks, P=0.05) but was not statistically different after adjustment, and gestational age at TOPFA was comparable.
The evidence is insufficient to definitively establish high-IQ schizophrenia as a clinically distinct subtype, although high-IQ patients show some distinguishing clinical features.

In a study of 29 schizophrenia patients with exceptionally high pre-morbid IQ (mean estimated IQ 120), about half had minimal post-onset IQ decline; compared with typical-IQ schizophrenia patients, they had significantly lower negative and disorganised symptoms (RRR=0.019; 95% CI=0.001–0.675, P=0.030) and better global functioning and insight (RRR=1.082; 95% CI=1.020–1.148; P=0.009), while those with minimal decline showed more manic symptoms (RRR=8.213; 95% CI=1.042–64.750, P=0.046).

Other supplied evidence links cognition and schizophrenia genetically and phenotypically (intelligence genetic variance 0.66; phenotypic covariance -0.38, with 89% shared genetic effects) but does not compare high-IQ subtypes, so the passages do not settle whether this is a distinct subtype.
No—among 7 people with type 1 diabetes and 10 controls who regularly ran more than 5 km, no Achilles tendon response to load was seen in either group over the 4 days after a 10 km run.
Baseline tendon structure was similar between groups, including UTC echo-types I–IV and anterior-posterior thickness (all p > 0.05).
Thus, in this small study, type 1 diabetes did not appear to affect Achilles tendon response to a 10 km run.

Yes, financial incentives appear cost-effective, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of £482 per QALY, though uncertainty remains. In a UK NHS analysis alongside an RCT, 612 pregnant women in Glasgow were randomized to usual cessation support plus or minus up to £400 in vouchers contingent on smoking cessation. The incremental cost per quitter at 34-38 weeks was £1127 ($1716), and the lifetime Markov model yielded an incremental cost of £17 and a 0.04 QALY gain, giving £482/QALY ($734/QALY). Probabilistic sensitivity analysis indicated uncertainty, particularly about relapse after birth, and the expected value of perfect information was £30 million at a willingness to pay of £30,000/QALY, so further research may be worthwhile. Other supplied studies address persistence of cessation after pregnancy and smoking trends, not cost-effectiveness.

Mixed: in a prospective single-centre study of 1829 attendances (40.7% admitted), triage nurses' admission probability estimate (VAS) was not better than the objective GAPS score overall, with comparable discrimination (AUC 0.876 for GAPS vs 0.875 for VAS, p=0.93) and accuracy (80.6% vs 79.0%, p=0.18).
However, nurses overestimated admissions (47.3% vs actual 40.7%, p<0.0001), whereas GAPS was well calibrated (41.0%, p=0.678).

In the majority of cases where nurses were not at least 95% certain, GAPS significantly outperformed nurses on calibration (+1.2% vs +9.2%, p<0.0001), discrimination (AUC 0.810 vs 0.759, p=0.001) and accuracy (75.1% vs 68.9%, p=0.0009).

When nurses felt at least 95% certain (a minority), their accuracy was excellent at 92.4%, and a strategy using GAPS but over-ruling it when clinical certainty was ≥95% outperformed either method alone (AUC 0.891, accuracy 82.5%).
In a study of 561 patients with misty mesentery on CT, 80 had isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7%, and 67.5% of all patients were obese and 17.5% overweight.
The other passages concern obesity and OSA/GERD, not misty mesentery.
No, viral co-infection did not influence the severity of acute respiratory infection in children, because the number of detected viruses did not correlate with any markers of severity.

In a Spanish prospective multicenter study of 204 children admitted with ARI, with a UK replication cohort of 97, viral co-infection was assessed by PCR detection of multiple viruses and compared to severity markers, and no correlation was found.

Bacterial superinfection, however, was associated with increased severity (OR 4.356; P=0.005), PICU admission (OR 3.342; P=0.006), higher clinical score (1.988; P=0.002), respiratory support (OR 7.484; P<0.001), and longer hospital stay (OR 1.468; P<0.001).
Yes, a qualitative study of MPH programs found considerable reported contributions to health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries, though with limitations.

In-depth interviews with 10 graduates per program, their peers, and supervisors from a distance MPH program in South Africa and a residential program in the Netherlands reported workplace impacts including promotion to leadership, expanded management roles, workplace innovations, teaching, advocacy, and community engagement.

Beyond the workplace, graduates had national reach through policy advisory roles to Ministries of Health, policy development, and capacity building, but work conditions and context influenced their effect and self-selection and social acceptability bias may have influenced findings.
No, the supplied evidence indicates risk calculators are not accurate for predicting surgical site occurrence (SSO) after open ventral hernia repair, with low areas under the curve (AUCs).
In a retrospective multicenter database (n=795; SSO rate 23%), the SSO AUCs were 0.56, 0.54, 0.52, and 0.60 for VHRS, VHWG, CDC wound class, and HW-RAT.
In a prospective single-center database (n=88; SSO rate 14%), the SSO AUCs were 0.63, 0.54, 0.50, 0.57, and 0.69.

Some models did stratify patients into groups with differing SSO rates (VHRS and HW-RAT retrospectively; ACS-NSQIP prospectively), but VHRS, VHWG, and CDC overestimated SSO risk while HW-RAT and ACS-NSQIP underestimated it.

The passages do not settle accuracy for surgical site occurrences outside open ventral hernia repair; one related passage notes that external validation of colorectal surgical site infection prediction models is lacking.
Yes—the supplied study found that aortic arch anatomy is associated with traumatic aortic injury severity.

In 22 TAI patients treated with TEVAR, mean aortic arch index and angle differed by injury type (type I: 6.8 cm and 58.3°; type III: 4.4 cm and 45.9°; type IV: 3.3 cm and 37°), with substantial differences between type III and IV.
Multivariate analysis confirmed that aortic arch angle was significantly associated with occurrence of type III damage (OR 1.5; 95% CI 1.03–2.2).
This is a small retrospective study, so it supports but does not definitively establish the relationship.

In a small randomized trial of 20 women at 16–23 weeks given 1 mg gemeprost vaginally every 6 hours, the median induction-to-abortion interval was 13 hours with paracervical block versus 20 hours without it, a non-significant difference.

Pethidine requirement and pain intensity, especially in late first stage, were not statistically different, and Butylscopolamine requirement was actually higher in the paracervical block group (p<0.05).
No side effects of paracervical anaesthesia occurred, but the small sample limits conclusions.
Yes, the retromandibular transparotid approach appears to be a reliable option for surgical treatment of condylar fractures based on a retrospective series of 25 patients.

In these patients, preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health were restored in most, esthetic outcomes were satisfactory, and there were no permanent neurologic impairments or major postoperative complications.
The study evaluated static and dynamic occlusal function, temporomandibular joint health, neurologic impairments, and esthetic outcomes with a minimum 1-year follow-up.
However, it was a single retrospective evaluation without a reported comparison group, so the evidence supports reliability but does not compare this approach to others.
Yes—populations with access to general practitioner (GP) hospitals used general hospitals less than populations without such access.

In an observational study of 35,435 admissions over five years in Finnmark, Norway, total general hospital admission rates were 26% lower for men and 28% lower for women in peripheral municipalities with a GP hospital compared with central municipalities without one.
Occupied bed days in general hospitals were 38% lower for men and 52% lower for women.
The differences were most pronounced for respiratory diseases, cardiac failure, cancer, stroke, and fractures.
This observational evidence shows an association, not definitive causation.

The evidence is mixed/insufficient: one prospective TEE study suggests that marginally acceptable hearts (fractional area change <50%) can be transplanted, but they may carry a trend toward worse survival and some risk of ventricular dysfunction. Among 55 potential brain-dead donors, 20 had FAC <50%; of 36 successful transplants, 9 recipients received hearts with donor FAC <50% (group H2) and 27 received hearts with FAC >50% (group H1), with four deaths including two from ventricular dysfunction in the FAC<50% group and actuarial survival of 86.2% vs 64.6% (p = NS) for H1 vs H2 at 1 and 2 years, respectively. Donor FAC increased significantly from 51±15% to 57±11% in 18 hearts reassessed in recipients, suggesting potential recovery, but the small sample and non-significant survival difference mean the passages do not settle suitability.
